rules.title: Vehicle traits
rules.text: A vehicle has five traits: Size, Strength, Speed, Defense and Toughness. Each costs equipment points to improve, much like a character trait. Size sets the starting Strength, Toughness and Defense; Strength sets how much the vehicle can haul; Speed is a movement effect; Defense is how hard it is to hit; Toughness is how much punishment it shrugs off.

rules.title: Vehicle trait costs
rules.text: Size: 1 point per size category above Medium (Medium is the free default). Strength: 1 point per +1 over the base for its size. Speed: the normal cost of the movement effect bought (Speed, Swimming and Burrowing 1 point per rank, Flight 2 points per rank). Defense: 1 point per point of size penalty bought off. Toughness: 1 point per +1 over the base for its size. Features: 1 point each. Powers: their normal power cost.

rules.title: Size categories
rules.text: Medium (motorcycle): Str 0, Tou 5, Defense penalty 0. Large (car, truck): Str 4, Tou 7, -2. Huge (stretch limo, SUV, tank): Str 8, Tou 9, -4. Gargantuan (semi, yacht, fighter jet): Str 12, Tou 11, -6. Colossal (passenger jet): Str 16, Tou 13, -8. Awesome (space transport): Str 20, Tou 15, -10. The book's vehicle list shows Defense as 10 plus this penalty (Medium 10, Large 8, Huge 6, Gargantuan 4, Colossal 2, Awesome 0).

rules.title: Cost formula (as DCUGen computes it)
rules.text: Cost = size cost (Medium 0, Large 1, Huge 2, Gargantuan 3, Colossal 4, Awesome 5) + (Strength - size base Strength) + movement effect cost x Speed rank + (Defense - (10 + size penalty)) + (Toughness - size base Toughness) + feature costs + power costs. Traits below the size baseline give no refund (the book's Bomber, with Strength 13 on a Colossal frame, is priced that way). Extra movement modes are Alternate Effects: +1 point each.

rules.title: Speed and movement modes
rules.text: A vehicle buys the movement effect that matches how it travels and pays its normal cost. A vehicle with several modes (land, sea and air, say) pays full price for the most expensive one and takes the rest as Alternate Effects for 1 point each. Speed rank converts to miles per hour the usual way (rank 5 is about 60 mph, rank 10 about 2,000 mph).

rules.title: Defense
rules.text: Bigger vehicles are easier to hit: size larger than Medium applies a penalty to the Defense attackers roll against, and the largest vessels can be hit with a routine check. Each -1 of that penalty can be bought off for 1 equipment point.

rules.title: Toughness and armor
rules.text: Size gives a base Toughness used for the vehicle's resistance checks; each +1 over it costs 1 point. Armor is Protection added to the vehicle at 1 point per +1 Toughness, and may be Impervious (as on tanks) or Sustained (force screens) instead of Permanent. Impervious Toughness costs 1 point per rank it covers.

rules.title: Standard equipment and features
rules.text: Seats, belts, climate control, a radio, lights and similar touches with no game effect come free. Features are optional extras at 1 point each, and the GM decides what counts as standard. Some features are really powers and cost what the power costs.

rules.title: Powers on vehicles
rules.text: Vehicle systems can be bought as power effects: attack effects for mounted weapons, defenses for armor and screens, sensory effects for cloaks and sensors. A vehicle power costs its normal power cost in equipment points, which is effectively one-fifth the power-point price for the owner. A partial modifier such as "Damage 10, Burst Area 8" adds +1 per rank for only the listed ranks.

rules.title: Environmental immunity
rules.text: A vehicle protects its occupants from the normal hazards of the medium it is built for (underwater, vacuum) at no extra cost. Pay for Immunity only for unusual protection, such as a sealed air supply in a car.

rules.title: Weapons
rules.text: Vehicle weapons are usually Damage with modifiers: machine guns are Ranged Multiattack Damage 6, a tank cannon Ranged Damage 10 with Burst Area on 6 ranks, air-to-air missiles add Homing. Weapons usable only one at a time can be Alternate Effects of the biggest (+1 point each), which is how the book prices military copters, fighter jets and space cruisers.

rules.title: Vehicles skill
rules.text: Vehicles (Dexterity, trained only) covers driving and piloting cars, boats, aircraft and spacecraft. Ordinary driving needs no check; roll only under pressure: chases, combat, or racing a deadline. Riding animals uses Expertise: Riding (Agility) with the same difficulties.

rules.title: Maneuvers
rules.text: Vehicles check DCs: 5 easy (a low-speed turn), 10 average (a sudden reverse, dodging obstacles), 15 difficult (tight turns), 20 challenging (bootlegger reverse, loop, barrel roll), 25 formidable (high-speed maneuvers, jumping or weaving around obstacles).

rules.title: Chases
rules.text: The book has no separate chase subsystem: run a chase as a series of opposed or DC-based Vehicles checks using the maneuver table, with Speed deciding who can catch whom. Features such as Oil Slick (pursuer makes DC 15 Vehicles check to keep control), Caltrops and Smokescreen exist to shake pursuers.

rules.title: Vehicle combat
rules.text: A driver uses the vehicle's weapons with his or her own attack check against the target's Defense; attackers roll against the vehicle's Defense (with its size penalty). Driving a vehicle normally takes a move action, including by Remote Control. Hits are resisted with the vehicle's Toughness like any object; an inanimate vehicle can be hit with a routine check or a normal check that counts as an automatic critical (+5).

rules.title: Ramming and collisions
rules.text: Treat ramming as a slam attack made with the vehicle: charge into the target, using damage equal to the vehicle's speed rank or its normal damage +1, whichever is higher, +1 more if it moved its full speed first. The rammer resists half that damage (rounded down) with its own Toughness. Slam damage is capped by power level. DCUGen applies the book's slam rules to vehicles, since the vehicle section has no separate collision table.

rules.title: Damaged vehicles
rules.text: Vehicles are equipment and take damage like objects, using their Toughness. Each time a vehicle is damaged it loses 1 feature or takes a -1 circumstance penalty on checks with it until repaired. Two degrees of failure against an attack meant to break it leaves a hole or breach; three or more wrecks it.

rules.title: Repairs
rules.text: Repairs use Technology. A vehicle is an advanced item (build DC 30, time rank 16 or about 4 days); repairing is DC 5 lower with time 2 ranks shorter (DC 25, about 1 day). A jury-rig is DC 10 below the build DC (DC 20), takes a standard action, fixes one problem and lasts until the end of the scene. Take -5 on the check to cut the time by one rank. A lost vehicle can be replaced with time and resources, since it is part of the owner's equipment.

rules.title: Equipment points
rules.text: Vehicles are bought with equipment points from the Equipment advantage: 5 points per rank. A shared team vehicle is paid for by the members in whatever split they agree, each devoting Equipment ranks to it.

rules.title: Alternate vehicles
rules.text: Since you can only drive one at a time, a character's vehicles are Alternate Equipment: pay full price for the most expensive and 1 point for each other vehicle of the same or lower cost. A hero point can produce a fitting spare vehicle for one scene.

rules.title: Book table inconsistencies
rules.text: Several printed costs on the DCA 158 table do not follow the book's own trait costs (for example the Police Cruiser is listed at 11 though it beats the 10-point Car by +1 Strength, +1 Speed and +1 Toughness). DCUGen keeps the printed price as book_cost, explains the gap in book_cost_note, and stores the cost the formula gives.

rules.title: Spaceships: drives
rules.text: Buy in-system speed as Flight (2 points per rank; Flight 12 is roughly 8,000 mph). Faster-than-light travel is a separate Movement power: Space Travel 1 reaches other planets in the system, 2 reaches other star systems, 3 reaches distant stars or other galaxies (2 points per rank). It only works in vacuum, so ships also need Flight for atmosphere and orbit.

rules.title: Spaceships: life support
rules.text: A spacecraft protects its crew from vacuum for free, because space is its normal environment. Buy Immunity only for extra protection: Immunity 10 (Life Support) for a lifeboat that must keep passengers alive anywhere, or a few ranks against radiation storms or alien atmospheres.

rules.title: Spaceships: shields and hulls
rules.text: Hull plating is the Toughness trait (1 point per +1), optionally Impervious Toughness. Energy shields are Protection with the Sustained extra (no cost change, but they can be switched off or nullified), or Impervious if the shields shrug off small arms. Keep total Toughness within what the series allows for vehicles.

rules.title: Spaceships: crews
rules.text: The vehicle sheet only prices the hull. Gunners, engineers and pilots are minions or ordinary NPCs; a large crew can be the Personnel of a mobile headquarters. Each weapon needs someone to fire it; one gunner per Alternate Effect array is a good rule of thumb.

rules.title: Spaceships: weapons
rules.text: Fighter blasters: Ranged Damage 10. Cruiser beams: Ranged Damage 12. Torpedoes: Ranged Damage 12-15 with Burst Area on 10-12 ranks and Homing 8. Point-defense: Ranged Multiattack Damage 6-8. Put weapons that one gunner fires into one array (Alternate Effects, +1 each).

rules.title: Spaceships: tractor beams
rules.text: A tractor beam is Move Object (2 points per rank, ranged): rank 10 hauls 25 tons, rank 14 about 400 tons. Add Limited (only toward the ship) to halve the price for a pure docking beam.

rules.title: Fantasy vessels: propulsion
rules.text: Rowed and animal-drawn craft just buy Speed or Swimming. Sails that need wind take Limited (needs wind) on their movement, halving its cost. Magical lift (a carpet, a sky-galleon's keel crystal, a witch's broom) is Flight, often with a flaw: Unreliable for temperamental magic, Limited (not over running water, only by night) for magic with a taboo.

rules.title: Fantasy vessels: enchantments
rules.text: Spells woven into a vessel are powers: a ghost ship's spectral form is Insubstantial 4, an elven skiff's silence is Concealment with Blending, a dragon team's fire is a Cone Area Damage. A ship that comes when called has Remote Control. A flying castle is an Awesome vehicle that can also serve as a headquarters bought separately.

rules.title: Fantasy vessels: crews and mounts
rules.text: Steeds that pull a vehicle are part of its Speed or Flight; if the beasts fight on their own, buy them as minions. Galley rowers, deckhands and ghostly crews are NPCs. Piloting a ship uses Vehicles; driving a team of animals can use Expertise: Riding at the same DCs.

rules.title: Steampunk vehicles
rules.text: Steam carriages, zeppelins, clockwork walkers and land ironclads use the normal rules. Boilers that need stoking can take Limited or Unreliable on movement; legged walkers add Leaping as a second movement mode (+1 point). Heavy riveted plate is Impervious Toughness, and gun decks are Ranged Damage with partial Burst Area.

features.name: Alarm
features.text: Sounds off at any unauthorized entry or start-up attempt. Technology DC 20 to defeat; each extra point raises the DC by 5.

features.name: Caltrops
features.text: Spike dispenser (standard action). Ordinary vehicles that drive over them lose their tires; a hero's or villain's vehicle makes a DC 13 Toughness check with tire Toughness 3: one degree of failure slows it, two immobilize it.

features.name: Hidden Compartments
features.text: Concealed cargo space for up to a tenth of the vehicle's medium load. Perception DC 20 to find; each extra point raises the DC by 5.

features.name: Navigation System
features.text: +5 circumstance bonus to navigation-related checks. The book's sample hero car takes it twice for +10 (DCA 213).

features.name: Oil Slick
features.text: Dumps a 20 by 20 ft. slick (standard action); a pursuing driver must make a DC 15 Vehicles check to keep control.

features.name: Remote Control
features.text: The owner can drive the vehicle by remote, using the same action as driving it from the seat (usually a move action).

features.name: Vehicle Armor
features.text: Protection on top of the vehicle's Toughness, 1 point per +1. DCUGen folds bought armor into the Toughness trait at the same price; use this entry for armor you want listed separately (for instance Sustained force screens).

features.name: Impervious Toughness
features.text: The Impervious extra on that many ranks of the vehicle's Toughness: damage of half that rank or less has no effect. 1 point per rank, no more ranks than its Toughness. Tanks have 6, APCs 4.

features.name: Cloaking Device (One Sense)
features.text: Concealment from normal vision, or from all of one other sense type such as radar or hearing (a stealth mode). 4 points. (The gear list in equipment.json calls this Concealment 4; the 4-point price is Concealment 2 at 2 points per rank.)

features.name: Cloaking Device (All Visual)
features.text: Concealment from all visual senses. 8 points. (The gear list in equipment.json calls this Concealment 8; the 8-point price is Concealment 4.)

features.name: Smokescreen
features.text: Releases thick smoke or mist that hides the vehicle and blinds pursuers: a Cloud Area visual Concealment Attack, priced by the book at 12 points like a smoke grenade.

features.name: Towing Cables
features.text: Cables or a winch to tow another vehicle or object up to the vehicle's Strength. Seen on a villain's submarine in the book.

features.name: Autopilot
features.text: Drives or flies itself on a set course with no check, freeing the pilot for other actions. Makes Vehicles checks with a +0 bonus if forced to.

features.name: Cargo Hold
features.text: Large secured cargo space; carries its full Strength in freight. Take again for a second bay or refrigeration.

features.name: Communications Suite
features.text: Radio, police-band scanner, encrypted team channel and video link; like the Communications headquarters feature in miniature.

features.name: Crew Quarters
features.text: Bunks, galley and stores for the crew to live aboard for weeks.

features.name: Ejection System
features.text: Ejector seats or escape capsules let everyone aboard bail out safely as a reaction when the vehicle is wrecked.

features.name: Laboratory Module
features.text: A compact lab: allows Expertise, Investigation and Technology checks that need a laboratory while on the move.

features.name: Luxury Quarters
features.text: Staterooms, a bar, fine furnishings: impresses passengers and grants a +2 circumstance bonus to Persuasion with guests aboard.

features.name: Medical Bay
features.text: Stretchers and trauma gear for full use of Treatment aboard; stabilizes passengers in transit.

features.name: Rescue Gear
features.text: Ladders, winches, hydraulic cutters and searchlights; +2 circumstance bonus to rescue-related checks.

features.name: Artificial Gravity
features.text: Gravity plating keeps the decks at about 1 g, so people aboard suffer none of the zero-g penalties and need no Environmental Adaptation inside the ship.

features.name: Armory
features.text: Weapon lockers and vacuum-rated armor for a boarding or landing party. The gear itself is bought as the characters' own equipment; this just means it is aboard and maintained.

features.name: Brig
features.text: Secure holding cells for prisoners (Technology DC 25 to break out of the locks, like a high-security vault). Take again for +5 DC each time or for a larger cell block.

features.name: Cold Sleep Bay
features.text: Suspended-animation pods: sleepers do not age, eat or breathe during the voyage. Waking takes a minute and leaves a sleeper fatigued for an hour. Take again for more pods (one rank per tenth of the ship's complement).

features.name: Docking Collar
features.text: Universal docking clamps and an extendable pressurized tube. Docking with a cooperating ship or station is routine; docking with a disabled one is DC 10 instead of 15.

features.name: Engineering Workshop
features.text: Machine shop, spare parts and fabricators: Technology checks to repair the ship (or build gear) aboard never suffer the -5 penalty for missing tools.

features.name: Fuel Scoop
features.text: Lets the ship refuel by skimming a gas giant, comet or star corona: a DC 15 Vehicles check and time rank 12 (8 hours) of skimming.

features.name: Hangar Bay
features.text: A launch bay for small craft: one rank holds a flight of up to four Huge or smaller craft (or one Gargantuan); take again for more. The craft are separate vehicles, bought on their own or run as minions.

features.name: Jump Computer
features.text: An astrogation computer that plots FTL jumps: jump checks can be made as routine checks (take 10) when not under pressure, and plotting never suffers the -5 no-tools penalty.

features.name: Recycling Life Support
features.text: Closed-loop air, water and food systems: the ship never runs out of consumables for its normal crew. Without it, a ship carries supplies for its endurance (see Supplies and fuel in the space rules).

features.name: Self-Destruct
features.text: A coded overload that destroys the ship after a countdown the captain sets. Anyone close enough when it blows faces a Burst Area Damage effect of the ship's Toughness rank.
